overrides.reason: Grooves into a FRUSTUM: a 90 or 200 degree groove whose outer wall is 0.4 to 0.5 mm inside a shallow frustum wall builds with volume off by 5.9e-4 to 3.2e-3 and 8 faces instead of 9 (OCCT and an independent integral agree with each other). Walls 0.1 mm either side are refused only by chance. The cone surface has no geometric guard. The box, post, tube, stepped-plate and sphere parts in this row were not shown wrong.

The overConstrained flag (absolute residual > 1e-3) is not a reliable report: its own evidence shows 5 false flags and 2 misses (residual up to 6e-4), and at scale 1e5, 28 of 40 satisfiable rectangles are flagged. Row 43 marks the same flag wrong, so the two rows contradicted each other.

addedRows.evidence: Guarded path builds 1 body and 9 faces where OCCT has 2 solids and 12 faces (two sides); four sides: volume 6869.80 against closed form 6867.26 (3.7e-4, bar 3e-4). No guard fires.

addedRows.feature: repeat/mirror of a pocket whose thin wall (0.15 mm or less) lies against the inner face of a notch, the underside of a notch edge, or the side of a joined boss (the thin-web guard compares walls with the part's bounding box only)

split.label: 20a
split.feature: pick after move() or a quarter turn of a primitive: hollow(open) after a non-copy move or a quarter turn of the primitive (the face is followed), and round/bevel(edge) on a primitive turned by whole quarter turns where its own frame and the world frame name the same edge
split.evidence: On the host (followMoves on) a named edge of a primitive turned by whole quarter turns is read two ways: in the primitive's own frame (the face parts turn with the body; solidcraft's labels do) and in the world frame (the face parts are world directions after the turn; what the OCCT and brep-rs referees read, brep-adapter topo-resolve.ts). It is built only where both name the same edge, or where the world frame names no face (a cylinder lying on its side has no world top or bottom face, so its own frame is the only reading); otherwise it is refused (resolve-names.ts turnedFrameClash). Hollow after a move: see move-turn row 2 (97 RIGHT, 0 wrong; real-kernel proof 221 right, 0 wrong). Edge after a quarter turn: fc corpus, every box case names two different edges, so all 21 are refused (20b), and the 3 in the move-turn corpus; the 8 turned-cylinder rim cases build (fillet-chamfer 18a).

split.label: 18a
split.feature: round/bevel(cylinder.edge(top|bottom, side),size) on a cylinder turned by whole quarter turns: supported where the primitive frame and the world frame name the same edge (a cylinder lying on its side has no world top or bottom face, so its own frame is the only reading)
split.evidence: On the host (followMoves on) a named edge of a primitive turned by whole quarter turns is read two ways: in the primitive's own frame (the face parts turn with the body; solidcraft's labels do) and in the world frame (the face parts are world directions after the turn; what the OCCT and brep-rs referees read, brep-adapter topo-resolve.ts). It is built only where both name the same edge, or where the world frame names no face (a cylinder lying on its side has no world top or bottom face, so its own frame is the only reading); otherwise it is refused (resolve-names.ts turnedFrameClash). fc corpus, both rigs: 8 of 8 built (r-cyl-turn-x90/y90 top-rim and bottom-rim-bevel, b-cyl-turn the same). Volume matches the group closed form and OCCT (4e-5, 1.1e-4) on all 8; the 4 top rims match OCCT's centre of mass to 2.4e-7. The 4 bottom-rim bevels are 1.45e-2 of the diagonal off OCCT's centre of mass, and that is an OCCT artefact: OCCT finds no cap facing world -z, its tie-break takes the local top cap for bottom as it does for top (its centre-of-mass shift is the same for both names), so it bevels the top rim; the build bevels the named bottom rim. Not a second-oracle confirmation of those 4: an owner review item.
